Commander O'Neil.title: Commander O'Neil
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or parried
Drops 12,000, Commander's Standard, Unalloyed Gold Needle
strat: Use any tanky Spirit Ash Summons, as they will likely draw the most attention from the boss and his allies.
Use the Rock Sling Spell, which can easily be obtained in the nearby ruins.
Bring equipment inflicting Frostbite or/and Hemorrhage.
Sneak up to O'Neil, which can be done with ease. This allows to perform few attacks before he even try to summon.
Riding Torrent during this fight is recommended to avoid Scarlet Rot build up
You can sneak up behind him and cast poison mist

O'Neil cannot jump, so you can summon Latenna or use ranged bows on a tree branch to whittle him down. His crossbow summons in phase 1 will knock Latenna off the branch however, and his phase 2 summons can kill her. It is also possible for her to slowly inch forward and fall down within reach of O'Neil.

Killing summoned Exile Crossbowmen and Exile Axe Soldiers is straightforward from horseback and can be performed without engaging with Commander O'Neil. Doing so will minimize the potential of being staggered or blindsided while attacking O'Neil and will simplify the fight. He will summon a second group of summons wielding axes during his second phase. Although they lack range, they will move towards you aggressively and will do more damage than the first group. However, they can also be dealt with relatively ...
If you want to beat him on foot, it is also doable, since most of his attacks are easily parryable. You just have to watch out for the summons and the Rot Storm.

You can kite him out to the nearby Site of Grace, then kite him through the Scarlet Rot geysers to damage him; he needs to be walking through the geyser when it erupts to take damage, the large pool of Scarlet Rot doesn't affect him. He will teleport back to the starting point for his second phase, and can be kited out to the geysers again. The second group of summons will likely follow him out, and that's a good time to use your Spirits to eliminate the summons.

Starscourge Radahn.title: Starscourge Radahn
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
Drops 70,000, Remembrance of the Starscourge, Radahn's Great Rune
strat: Torrent is available for this fight (unless other players are summoned in for co-op)
With the summons, it is possible (if slow) to complete the fight without attacking Radahn directly.
These can be blocked with a shield, but will do heavy magic damage. They will kill most players in one hit.

The arrows home so accurately that they are usually not possible to dodge without the use of i-frames, such as rolling or mounting/dismounting Torrent. As always, rolling toward the source of a projectile will make it easier to dodge.
Debris on the battlefield will block the arrows once, as the arrow will destroy the debris instead of hitting the player. The first two groups of summon signs are behind such debris.

A reliable approach is to raise your shield when you enter the arena and approach the first group of summon signs. Summon all available NPCs, using the debris next to their signs for cover, and advance to the next group with your shield up. Keep an eye on Radahn: at some point he pulls back his bow without the magical energy charges, signaling you to get on your horse and begin strafing to avoid his spear-arrow attacks. Once you get close enough, Radahn will pull out his swords and begin his melee attacks, at ...

If the player stays a far enough distance away, he will become unable to perform his arrow wall attack, making the opening sequence of the fight a lot easier. In terms of proximity, avoid going past the first 3 summon signs you see until one of them has had the opportunity to make Radahn switch to his Melee stance. After which you are fine to continue moving forward and collect the missing summon signs.

Otherwise, if you don't want to deal with Radahn's ranged attacks, there's also a way to prevent them altogether. As soon as you load into the arena, start running away in the opposite direction until Radahn's model is unloaded. When the model is no longer visible on screen, start heading back towards him; as he reappears, Radahn will automatically pull out the swords and will start approaching you in melee mode, giving you more than enough time to safely buff or summon the phantoms without the arrows bothering ...

Almost all of Radahn's ranged attacks, including his magic arrow and both of his magic rock and sphere projectiles will likely kill in one hit. The magic arrows are best dodged with i-frames or blocked. The magic rocks and magic spheres can be dodged with i-frames or by sprinting perpendicularly to Radahn on Torrent.

Radahn is extremely weak to Scarlet Rot. Inflicting it on him once will bring him down to half health in a short time. Inflicting it on him again near the start of the second phase will kill him in a short time. By far the easiest way to win the fight is to hit him with Rotten Breath, which will require two successful hits to inflict Scarlet Rot.
Suggested weapon: Antspur Rapier (DEX/ARC)

In the first phase of the battle, Radahn moves around quickly on horseback, making it challenging to land consistent hits. Fast weapons with bleed effects, such as the Uchigatana, Bloodhound's Fang, or Hookclaws, are particularly effective. The summoned NPCs will often draw Radahn’s attention, allowing you to land several chain attacks. Bleed builds up quickly, dealing significant damage, but be cautious when Radahn's health drops to around 75%. At this point, he'll clang his two Greatswords together and slam them ...
Phase 1.5: 75% HP

In Phase 1.5, Radahn gains a few new ranged attacks, but the fight remains similar to the first phase. Some NPCs may die, but they can be re-summoned after a short cooldown. Watch out for his rush attacks, and continue dealing damage in small bursts, retreating to heal on horseback when necessary.
Phase 2: 50% HP

During Phase 2, Radahn leaps into the air and seemingly vanishes, giving you a brief moment to heal and re-summon fallen allies. However, keep an eye on the sky, as he will come crashing back down like a fiery meteor. This can be dodged on horseback, but getting hit will likely result in instant death. Upon landing, Radahn summons four boulders that surround him and shoot toward you at high speed, potentially insta-killing you if you're not using a Greatshield. These boulders fire just before he uses his drill ...

For the rest of the fight, focus on re-summoning NPCs, as it’s too risky to engage Radahn directly. Many of his attacks deal heavy damage, so only strike when you see a clear opportunity. Radahn has three different AoE attacks to watch for: Gravitas Pull, which has a massive range and can pull you toward him (though it can be dodged); Gravitas Wave, where he jumps into the air and slams down, releasing a massive energy wave in a cone (which can be rolled through or jumped over on horseback); and Drill Blades, ...

Loretta's Greatbow can also be very effective while on horseback, although it does take much longer to cast. Magic Glintblade is a safer, faster alternative, but be wary that overzealous casting can trap you in your casting animation, leaving you easy prey for Radahn.

It is recommended to avoid using Thops' Barrier. It will reduce the damage of certain magical attacks, but will still force the player prone after the attack, leading to Radahn almost definitely killing the player anyways. Thops' Barrier will not work what-so-ever on the arrows, and his multi-Gravitas will deal less damage but leave the player prone. It is currently unknown if Thops' Barrier has any effect on Radahn's quad-Rock Sling attack.

Horseback cheese: Radahn is a unique shardbearer boss for two reasons. One, allies from the festival can be summoned an unlimited number of times. Two, Torrent can be used in the arena. These mechanics can be cheesed to make this fight relatively easy. Radahn has a high number of melee and AoE strikes, but not many ranged attacks. By using summons to keep him busy, you can ride around hitting him with projectiles causing poison, bleed, or other ailments to chunk down his HP. If you keep a safe distance and watch ...

Decaying Ekzykes.title: Decaying Ekzykes
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
Defeating Decaying Ekzykes unlocks Ekzykes's Decay at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid
strat: Ekzykes is extremely weak to Fire, so any fire damage you have (including Fire Grease) will be highly effective
Use Uchigatana or another weapon that inflicts Hemorrhage, since Ekzykes is vulnerable to both Hemorrhage and Slash it and it will do a substantial portion of its very large health pool
Use spells with very long range such as Loretta's Greatbow
Use Torrent to quickly escape the rot breath and even to double-jump over it without taking damage
Bring Preserving Boluses to get rid of rot buildup

Fight the Feet: As for Flying Dragon Agheel, most of Ekzykes's attacks can be dodged by running towards its feet. However, because its Stomp attacks kick up scarlet rot, it's more dangerous to stay underneath. To make a foot-focused strategy work, get in a few hits and then head back in front of the dragon. Once it does another attack, you can run back in to the feet and start the process over again.

A Song of Ice & Fire: Ekzykes is extremely weak to fire and moderately weak to Frostbite, so if you alternate between freezing him and hitting him with a large burst of flame you can deal a lot of damage. Faith builds can use Frozen Lightning Spear or Dragonice to freeze and O, Flame! to burn. Intelligence builds can use Freezing Mist or Glintstone Icecrag to freeze and Magma Shot to burn.

Flying Dragon Agheel.title: Flying Dragon Agheel
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
After taking a critical hit, takes an additional 20% standard damage for the rest of the fight
Defeating Agheel unlocks Agheel's Flame at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid
strat: Kaiden Sellsword Ashes can get in a good bit of damage before vanishing
Use Torrent to quickly close distance when Agheel flies away and more easily dodge its breath attacks
Be cautious when summoning a player for co-op. In addition to increasing the boss's HP, co-op will prevent you from riding Torrent
Try to hit its head whenever possible for bonus damage
Use Rock Sling for its high stance damage
Use Dragonwound Grease for 30% bonus damage

Heads Up: Agheel's head takes bonus damage, so focus on trying to land hits on it. Spears and Great Spears are great weapon options, since dragons are weaker to pierce damage, but anything with long reach will do. Stand in front of the boss—most of its forward-facing attacks can be punished with a hit on the head (see Attacks & Counters for details). Its most dangerous attacks from this position are Strafe and Retreat, so if you see it fly up into the air with fire at its mouth start running as quickly as you can. ...

Footsies: Many of Agheel's attacks can be avoided by simply running towards its feet. Although they don't take as much damage as its head, they're much easier to get in hits on. If you're going for this strategy, it's important to learn the timing of its High and Low Stomp attacks—if you can reliably jump attack over the shockwaves, you'll be able to keep up the pressure even when the dragon tries to punish you for staying out of range of its bites. You'll still need to be ready to run as soon as it starts a ...

Shield Up: If you are on foot, bring a good shield for your right hand. It'll be a lot harder for you to get out of the way when Agheel really wants to close in on you, so being able to block a physical attack as a backup option will help keep you alive.

Demi-Human Chief.title: Demi-Human Chief
facts: Closest Site of Grace: Coastal Cave
Multiplayer is available for this fight
You can summon Spirit Ashes for this boss
NPC Summons: Old Knight Istvan, as long as he's still alive
This boss guards the way to the Church of Dragon Communion
Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or parried
This fight features two Demi-Human Chiefs, both of which must be defeated to win the fight
This fight features several Demi-Humans as well, but only the Chiefs needs to be defeated to win
strat: Try to fight one Demi-Human Chief at a time. The second one is around a corner, so if you stay near the entrance to the boss room you can usually avoid attracting its attention.
Clear out the other Demi-Humans first with ranged attacks or spells.
Demi-Human Chiefs have low poise, so your attacks will usually interrupt theirs. Use this to chain multiple attacks or prevent yourself from getting hit.

Shielding: A decent shield can block most individual attacks, but you may not have enough stamina to fully block some combos. Once you've blocked the first attack, either dodge out of the way or guard counter to interrupt the next attack.

Bide Your Time: Wait for Knife Slam attack, when the Demi-Human Chief's knives will be briefly stuck in the floor. This is your opportunity to strike. Take advantage of their low poise to hit three or four times, as long as you still have enough stamina to retreat afterwards.

Shielding: Keep a in one hand and your catalyst or seal in the other so that you can block if needed. The Demi-Human Chiefs' attacks can have unexpected timings, so it's not always easy to dodge every attack.

facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or parried
strat: The Best Tips for Soldier of Godrick:
Soldier of Godrick is easy to defeat and you won't need to gain any advantage against him.
His attacks are very vertical: he swings his sword down to the ground and then up to the air, so dodge to the sides to avoid getting hit.
His poise is higher than his mob counterparts, so weapons with a high poise damage might be useful.
Soldier of Godrickhas a heavy sword, so it's easy to see his moves coming. The only tricky thing about him is that he looks like he is going to strike once, but he may suddenly perform a 3 hit combo.

Go Berserk: If you have enough health, simply attacking him repeatedly will be enough to defeat him even if you take several hits in the process. This strategy isn't advised, though, since this boss is a great chance to practice more advanced moves like guard counters, parrying, and dodging.

Charge and Crit: A charged heavy attack from any weapon will break his stance, allowing a critical hit that will deal about 30% of his total HP. You can prepare another heavy attack while he's getting up to break his posture again.
Guard Counters: The most foolproof way to defeat him is to hold up your shield and guard counter once he hits you. A single guard counter will break his stance, letting you get a critical hit.
Resort to Melee: Since Soldier of Godrick runs towards you and early spells take a long time to cast, it may be best to just equip your melee weapon for now and use one of the strategies above.

Bait and Blast: If you want to stick to magic, keep your distance as best as possible and bait him into using slow attacks. After you dodge, you'll have a chance to cast a single spell before repeating the process.

Bloodhound Knight Darriwil.title: Bloodhound Knight Darriwil
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
strat: Staunching Boluses can help prevent Hemorrhage
The Glintblade Phalanx spell and Ash of War can decimate this boss.
Use Guard Counters, but be careful as he often uses follow-up attacks and Hemorrhage can build up quickly.

Keep Your Guard Up: While you're still learning his moves, guard when you're not attacking so he doesn't dash in and surprise you with an unexpected attack. A Greatshield is particularly effective here, since most of his attacks will bounce off it and give you a chance to guard counter. Be aware though that he'll still build up Hemorrhage even if you perfectly block his attacks. Try to bait his attacks when your Hemorrhage buildup is low, block one or two attacks before attacking, then back away and try to dodge ...

Watch For Sparks: Pay particular attention to Darriwil's Grinding Attack and Clawing Attack, where he scrapes his blade or claw along the ground to create sparks. Both of these take him some time to recover from, so after you've dodged or blocked the initial attack you'll have a chance to land a hit or two.

Let It Bleed: When your Hemorrhage meter fills up, you'll take 100 damage plus 10% of your total health. But since this fight comes early in the game, that's not actually much more than a normal attack would deal. It may be worth simply taking the damage, especially if you're blocking the rest of his attacks, and focusing on killing Darriwil rather than saving yourself.

Form a Phalanx: Take advantage of Darriwil's aggression using Glintstone Phalanx which will slam into him approaches to attack. Summon the blades when you've got some distance, then when he gets close focus on not getting hit and let the magic do its work. Ash of War: Glintblade Phalanx may be an even better choice since it costs less FP and deals more Stance damage.

Fake Melee: Close-range spells like Carian Slicer or Catch Flame avoid the dodging issue entirely by only attacking him when he's close by. This will require carefully sequencing your dodges and attacks, though, to make sure you aren't just trading hits.

Jump and Shoot: If you're using a bow, avoid using slow skills like Mighty Shot since he's likely to dodge them. Instead, jump backwards when he approaches and fire an arrow while you're in the air to avoid his attacks and get in some damage.

Lichdragon Fortissax.title: Lichdragon Fortissax
facts: 60% Stance damage absorption on body, 20% on head
Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
strat: Recommended to use Mimic Tear Ashes, as it can tank fairly well and draw aggro away. Greatshield Soldiers can be a decent alternative, though they do not deal as much damage.
Use spells and incantations that summon large numbers of projectiles or hit multiple times, such as Rock Sling, Meteorite of Astel, Rotten Breath, or Comet Azur.
Bring Lightningproof Dried Livers, Boiled Crab, and Rejuvenating Boluses.
Equip the Prince of Death's Cyst or Pustule or reduce Death Blight buildup.
Like all Ancient Dragons, you can only lock onto the head and body, so it is recommended to not lock on and attack the legs instead.

Fortissax is most consistently and most safely fought by standing in front of the head and punishing Fortissax's various attacks. While it is possible to defeat it by running under and hacking at the ankles, a strategy also highly effective against Lansseax, Fortissax's lightning barrier renders this style of play significantly more risky. Not only does it make the fight slower by forcing you to dodge or sprint constantly to avoid being struck by the dropped charges, but it can combine unfavorably with other ...

To prepare for this fight, focus on items that boost your defenses against lightning. Boiled Crab, Lightningproof Dried Liver, and (Golden) Lightning Fortification are especially valuable. Avoid using Fireproof Dried Liver or other anti-fire buffs, as they don't stack, and fire is the least threatening of Fortissax's attacks.
If you're struggling with Death Blight, consider equipping the Prince of Death's Pustule for extra resistance. An upgraded version can be found in the Deeproot Depths where you fight Fortissax.

For weapons, choose one with strong thrust attacks. Fortissax is highly vulnerable to Thrust damage, and you can punish his rearing firebreath and double bite attacks for extra damage. Equip armor with high Lightning resistance and consider talismans like the Pearldrake Talisman, Boltdrake Talisman, and Dragoncrest Shield Talisman/Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman to reduce the damage from his powerful attacks.

Fortissax is resistant to lightning and holy damage, so use weapons that deal physical damage with fire, magic, or status effects. Dexterity builds using lightning-infused weapons should switch to Keen affinity, and faith builds might opt for unique weapons that scale non-holy damage, such as the Erdsteel Dagger, Magma Wyrm's Scalesword, or the Magma Whip Candlestick.

Don’t forget to consume the Baldachin's Blessing Fia gave you, as it reduces your max HP by 5% while in your inventory. Lastly, use Crystal Tears such as Shrouding Cracked Tears, Spiked Cracked Tear, and Opaline Bubbletear or Hardtear for this encounter.

Once you have entered the arena by interacting with Fia, Fortissax will begin the battle by summoning Death Lightning. Buff up with your chosen items, then run up to Fortissax and begin attacking one of the forearms. While you do, turn the camera behind you and identify areas where few lightning bolts will strike. When this move ends, put your back to those areas as you begin to fight Fortissax in earnest. You will be moving backwards more or less continually as you dodge the attacks and stay in front of ...

Once you have brought Fortissax to 60% HP, the moveset will change in two ways. First, Fortissax will gain two new attacks: a version of lightning spear where Fortissax summons two bolts and slams them sequentially into the ground, and a divebomb with a lightning glaive that ends in a double spin with the weapon extended. And secondly, the combos of Fortissax can now be extended. Initially, Fortissax's double bite had only a single possible followup (rearing fire breath), and his vertical slam had none. In phase ...

In summary: use items and equipment that increase lightning and/or physical absorptions, use thrust damage if possible and avoid using holy or lightning damage, stand in front of Fortissax and punish vertical slams and double bites, plan retreats through sparsely struck areas during Death Lightning summons, and be wary of moveset changes once Fortissax reaches 60% HP

Valiant Gargoyle (Twinblade).title: Valiant Gargoyle
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
Damage: Standard (Halberd), Standard, Slash, Holy (Greatsword), Standard, Pierce (Twinblade)
strat: Use the Spirit Jellyfish, Ancestral Follower, or any other ashes able to draw aggression away from you.
Use Pest Threads, as their large size means they can be hit multiple times for larger damage. Lightning Spear or Great Glintstone Shard are other ranged alternatives.
Use Incantation Flame, Cleanse Me or Cure Poison to cure yourself of poison buildup.
Melee users: Dodge roll to directly underneath/behind the gargoyle where it's attacks more seldom connect.
Melee users: Utilize a shield with Barricade Shield to tank some of the gargoyles blows.
A flask with Greenburst Crystal Tear will give better stamina recovery for blocking and dodge rolling.
If using the Mimic Tear ash summon, consider equipping yourself (and mimic) with the Kindred of Rot Talisman, which will boost attack power by 20% when poisoning occurs.

We can look at the encounter as having 3 phases: Phase 1 being a 1v1 fight against the first Gargoyle only, Phase 2 being a 1v2 against both Gargoyles, and Phase 3 being a 1v1 against the remaining Gargoyle. The goal in this encounter should be to take as little damage as possible in Phase 1, quickly burn down the low health Gargoyle in Phase 2, and then have enough Flask charges to get through Phase 3.

Prior to fighting this boss, the player may want to consider having a decently upgraded Flask, a way to cure Poison and decent damage output. If you attempt this fight with low damage, you may have problems with Phase 2, when both Gargoyles are ganging up on you. Also consider having a weapon with high range in order to hit the Gargoyles properly, this can be especially effective combined with playing with the camera unlocked. You may find that ranged summons such as the Spirit Jellyfish Ashes are good for this ...
Phase 1 (Sword Gargoyle)

In this phase, the goal is to simply take as little damage as possible. There is no timer, as the Twinblade Gargoyle comes into the fight when the Sword Gargoyle is around half health. Take your time to learn its attacks, most of them are relatively easy to dodge on reaction. You can be relatively aggressive in this phase if you learn the patterns, letting you get a potential stagger and consequently a critical hit coming into Phase 2. The Gargoyle will swap between its sword and halberd periodically, both of them ...

It is possible to stay quite close to the Gargoyle most of the time, just watch out for the Poison Mist attack it will use at close range. If you see it coming out, you have plenty of time to simply sprint away from the Gargoyle, and you will not take any damage. You can try to get free hits on the Gargoyle while it is spawning the mist, but be careful that you do not get poisoned. The safe bet is to simply run away and wait for a different opening.

Before the Sword Gargoyle hits half health, make sure to position it around the entrance to the boss arena. This will ensure that the Twinblade Gargoyle will spawn on the other side of the arena, giving you precious time to finish off the Sword Gargoyle before the Twinblade Gargoyle is able to make its way to you.
Phase 2 (Both Gargoyles)

Depending on your weapon and level of aggression, it is possible to get a stagger on the Sword Gargoyle right as Phase 2 is coming up. This is optimal, since it will give you a large burst of damage on the Sword Gargoyle. If your weapon has a good weapon art (such as The Queen's Black Flame), you may even want to use the weapon art instead of taking the critical hit.

Regardless of whether or not you get a stagger, make sure you use your highest damage output right after the Twinblade Gargoyle spawns. The optimal scenario is to fully kill the Sword Gargoyle before the Twinblade Gargoyle makes it to your position. Do not be afraid to trade hits with the Sword Gargoyle to make this happen, just watch out to not get flanked by the Twinblade Gargoyle. This is the hardest part of the fight, so doing everything in your power to end it quickly will greatly reduce the difficulty of ...

If you don't manage to kill off the Sword Gargoyle before the Twinblade Gargoyle gets to you, don't worry, you will simply have to play a bit differently from now on. If the Sword Gargoyle is not dead, it should at least be low on health. At this point, simply kite both of them and wait for openings to get hits in on the Sword Gargoyle. Try to keep both of them on your screen, and don't be afraid to take your time. It's worth noting that only one gargoyle usually attacks at a time, and it is usually the one ...
Phase 3 (Twinblade Gargoyle)

In the last part of this fight, you will only face the Twinblade Gargoyle, who will periodically swap between a Twinblade and a Greataxe. Its Twinblade moveset can be rather hard to read, so don't be afraid to simply wait it out until it swaps to the Greataxe. You can survive the Twinblade phase just by rolling away from it during most of its attacks. Most of the Greataxe moveset is much easier to read, and is more similar to the Sword Gargoyle's Halberd moveset. The Twinblade Gargoyle still has some very nasty ...

Ranged attacks are especially beneficial when both gargoyles are present to try to handle them both from a distance and avoid receiving damage. Try to keep them both in view to avoid any unexpected attacks from one or the other. You don't want to be unaware while a gargoyle is spewing extra poison into the arena or be unprepared for when they perform a lunge and close the distance very quickly. Focus ono clearing the first gargoyle so you can use phase 3 to focus on the twinblade gargoyle.

Mohg, Lord of Blood.title: Mohg, Lord of Blood
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
Buff is not applied, when blood loss happens during critical hit.
Drops 420,000, Mohg's Great Rune, Remembrance of the Blood Lord
strat: The player can find the Mohg’s Shackle item in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds under Leyndell just before the Leyndell Catacombs Site of Grace at the bottom of the pipe/water area. Can be used similar to Margit’s Shackle during the boss fight to tether him for a short bit. You will NOT be able to tether him once he has reached the health threshold for second phase; use it while he is just above that to give yourself a generous window to burst him down.

Mohg will recite Tres, Duo and Unus at certain health thresholds, placing a red ring around the player. At the start of his second phase, he will chant Nihil three times, doing large damage and healing himself for each ring on the player. In order to survive this attack, you will need a physick with the Purifying Crystal Tear, or will need to heal with crimson flasks. The damage will interrupt the player, so the optimal time to use the wondrous physick is before Mogh begins his phase transition countdown.

The Purifying Crystal Tear will provide the player with a shield, which prevents all three counts of bleed in the mid-battle attack described above. This is obtained by defeating the NPC invader Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger.
Equip fire and physical damage reduction to aid survival.
The Lord of Blood's Exultation will provide a substantial damage boost for a lot of the fight, given the numerous hemorrhage opportunities on either side.

If you can, aim to burst through his first phase as he takes his time counting down to the phase change. If you manage to stagger him before he actually uses Bloodboon Ritual, it's possible to kill him without seeing phase 2.

One of his signature moves is "Bloodflame Talons," which involves a quick slash followed by an explosive burst. Players should roll away at the moment of detonation to avoid the attack. Another dangerous move is "Bloodboon," where Mohg launches a splash of bloodflame that ignites the ground and inflicts hemorrhage. This attack can come in a wide arc, a narrow cone, or a shower, depending on the situation.

Mohg also employs spear attacks such as "Spear Swings," which consist of slow horizontal swipes that can be avoided by rolling forward with each swing. The "Thrust" involves a spear thrust into the ground, followed by a tug, which players can dodge by rolling past the thrust and attacking from behind.

Mohg has airborne assaults like "Assault," where he throws bloodflame before charging, and "Blood Tax," which inflicts damage and builds hemorrhage. Players should roll to the sides to evade these attacks.

Mohg also heavily relies on causing bleed buildup on the player with his bloodflame, especially during Phase 2. It is highly recommended the player boost their robustness and prepare consumables that will help mitigate bleed.
Players can also obtain Mohg's Shackle to stun him twice during Phase 1. Mohg's Shackle has no effect during Phase 2.

Upon entering the boss arena, the player has more than enough time to buff and use consumables before Mohg comes into attacking range. If the player wishes to maximize their buff duration, it is perfectly acceptable to start buffing after entering the fog gate.

For melee users with fast weapons, there are opportunities to land quick hits between his swings and then dodge the next attack. Slower weapon users, however, should wait until Mohg finishes his combo before attacking, as the delay between his attacks isn't long enough to swing and dodge safely.

During this phase, Mohg also uses limited Bloodflame moves, such as throwing Bloodflame or casting Bloodflame Talons. While these spells cause bleed buildup, they're highly telegraphed, and players shouldn't expect significant bleed damage in Phase 1.

Mohg also uses some limited Bloodflame movesets during this phase, mainly throwing Bloodflame at the player or using the Bloodflame Talons spell. While these spells all cause bleed buildup when they connect with the player, they are also highly telegraphed and players should not expect to take significant bleed damage during Phase 1.

One of the biggest challenges for melee players trying to stance break Mohg is his Bloodflame pools, which he summons defensively. This move can prevent players from attacking without taking damage, and repeated use of the Bloodboon can cause any stance damage dealt to decay, making stance breaking difficult.

Finally, throughout Phase 1, Mohg applies up to three Blood Curse stacks (Tres/Duo/Unus). Each time he applies a stack, he swings his trident to his right, so players should stay on his left side and deal as much damage as possible during these moments.

Mohg also makes heavy use of his wings during this phase, the most notable movesets being his plunging attack and his swooping attack. Of these, the plunging attack is especially devastating as it deals heavy damage and is also followed up by a delayed explosion. Players will have an easier time dodging his plunging attacks by simply strafing to the side instead of rolling, as it appears that he adjusts his landing position specifically to catch rolls.

At the site of grace ensure you mix the Purifying Crystal Tear, and the Speckled Hardtear into your Wonderous Physick Mix, both of which will mitigate some of the difficulty in his second phase. Regardless of the benefit of your Physick, though, this fight is going to be TOUGH, and the only way to survive is with high maneuverability. The flame and blood attacks both melt through your HP regardless of armor, so make sure you're at least light enough to avoid the fat roll here. Obviously, we'll want to use a spirit ...

Putting this into practice: The second you walk through the fog-gate, you need to 1: summon your spirit ash, 2: drink your physick, and 3: ready Mohg's Shackle (detailed above). Ideally you'd want to use the first of shackle's two charges before Mohg can launch his first attack, allowing you and your ash to wail on him, get a level of frostbite or bleed, and begin ticking down his stance. Then when you've cut Mohg's health down to about 60% or so, you'll want to use this again. The shackle only works in the first ...

This is where the maneuverability really comes into play, and why it's so important to reduce his health as much as possible before his second phase is triggered. The big thing here is dodging through his reaching attacks, not away from them, getting one or two hits in, then dodging laterally out of the range of his close range attacks before ultimately retreating. Otherwise the same strategy as the first phase (minus the shackle) applies here. Try and stance break him, and try to mix those two status effects.
The majority of spells will work well here, even those with long windup times. Some notable spells are the usual Glintstone Pebble variants like Glintstone Cometshard or Comet.
Mohg is extremely aggressive in close-quarters combat in both phases, so using spells like Carian Slicer or Carian Greatblade may be more dangerous than usual.

Carian Retaliation, both the Ash of War and the spell itself, are not recommended unless you can consistently parry some of his physical attacks with the Ash of War. However, using Cuckoo Glintstones and Glintstone Scraps and then using Carian Retaliation on the created projectiles does produce effective results. Thops' Barrier may be a preferable alternative against his Bloodflame sprays if you struggle with dodging these.

Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing (Boss).title: Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing (Boss)
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being parried
Is vulnerable to a backstab critical
Damage: Standard, Strike, Magic, Fire, Holy
Inflicts: Scarlet Rot (if Malenia has been killed), Hemorrhage (if Mohg, Lord of Blood has been killed)
Weapons: Scepter of the All-Knowing, Carian Glintblade Staff with No Skill (right), Finger Seal with No Skill (left)
Armor: All-Knowing Helm, All-Knowing Armor, All-Knowing Gauntlets, All-Knowing Greaves

Spells: Comet, Carian Phalanx, Black Flame Ritual, Law of Causality, Rykard's Rancor (if Rykard has been killed), Bloodboon (if Mohg, Lord of Blood has been killed), Scarlet Aeonia (if Malenia has been killed)
Drops 150,000, All-Knowing Set, Scepter of the All-Knowing
strat: The Best Tips for Sir Gideon Ofnir, The All-Knowing:
Use the Eternal Darkness spell to redirect nearly all his spells
Alternatively, Frenzied Burst can prove useful due to long range.
Recommended weapon: Erdtree Greatshield
Use Spirit Ashes that can quickly close the distance and harass Gideon such as Black Knife Tiche.
Use heavy jump attacks to disrupt Gideon's more powerful spells as he channels them.

Gideon has access to both Sorceries and Incantations and he can deal a huge amount of damage in a very short time. However, as a magic-focused boss, he is also easily interrupted. His more advanced spells such as Rykard's Rancor and Comet Azur require some channeling and a well-timed heavy jump attack will cause him to plop facedown on the ground, interrupting his cast.

Another weakness of Gideon is that nearly all of his attacks are projectiles that can be blocked by terrain and it just so happens there are several pillars conveniently placed on either side of his chamber. Make good use of these pillars, particularly for the same two spells noted above and you should be able to own this fight.

One attack of note for melee players to watch out for is his Black Flame Ritual which comes out really quickly and can shred HP in mere seconds. Make sure you are dodging out of range of this as soon as you see the black flames.

Magic users who are specc'd for the Eternal Darkness spell can near-trivialize this fight. Eternal Darkness creates a void orb that sucks in all projectile-based enemy spells, effectively rendering them useless. This includes his all-powerful Comet Azur beam. Do note that the projectiles can still hit you if you are in their path as they travel towards the void so make sure you are casting Eternal Darkness on one side and moving a few steps away to the side as you pummel Gideon with your own spells.
Eternal Darkness is not a fool-proof plan, however. It has a short duration and you should still be aware of Gideon's most dangerous attacks and use the pillars to your advantage.
Tiche and you combined can stunlock him without bothering with Eternal Darkness. Adula's Moonblade can be effective, or use fast spells to compensate for his tendency to dodge.
For Faith, Madness related spells - most notably Frenzied Burst - are useful.

Godfrey, First Elden Lord.title: Godfrey, First Elden Lord
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
strat: Mainly deals Standard Damage, so prioritize defence towards that type of damage.
No matter the build, during phase 1 it is important to keep close. He will otherwise dash towards you and Stomp, covering the entire area in AoE.
In phase 2, recognize his grapple patterns.
Alternatively, skills/spells that keeps player above ground can be used to avoid damage and inflict it at the same time.
His roar buffs and successful grab moves are slow, what player can use to cast Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike at point-blank for massive damage.

Most of his stomp moves can be avoided by jumping as soon as you see him lower his leg. The regular stomp travels in a cone in front of him, leaving him briefly vulnerable to attacks — just avoid being caught on the wider side of the cone.

Godfrey can also empower his stomps. When he stands at a distance, raises his axe overhead, and slowly lifts his leg, he’ll emit a red aura. While this effect lasts, the shockwaves from his stomps will cover the entire arena.
At around 50% HP, a cutscene triggers where Godfrey sheds his armor, slays his regent Serosh, and reveals his true form as Hoarah Loux, Warrior.

As Hoarah Loux, he switches to hand-to-hand grappling, abandoning his axe. The key to defeating him is recognizing the patterns of his grapples and dodging accordingly. His attacks as Hoarah Loux can one-hit players with low Vigor and bypass shields. The best openings to damage him are after he finishes an attack chain or leap attack. Fortunately, his health bar doesn’t refill when he reveals his true form, so you only need to deal with the last half of his health bar.

Sorcery users can start the fight with Terra Magica, followed by Rennala's Full Moon. Comet Azur can be risky, as Godfrey might open with a jump attack if the player isn't in range. Speed is more important than damage here, especially in phase 2, so good choices would be Comet/Glintstone Cometshard or Glintstone Icecrag.

As for Incantations, you can start the first phase with Borealis's Mist. This will provoke the First Elden Lord to perform an attack, often a stomp, but you should be safe during casting the incantation. It might be worth trying the same in the second phase, although Hoarah Loux's attack patterns makes this risky. During the second half of each phase, a fast spell like Lightning Spear is the best choice to chip away his health. Roar buffs can be used to approach him carefully, then cast charged Ancient Dragons' ...

Radagon of the Golden Order.title: Radagon of the Golden Order
facts: Parryable: Yes, but 3 parries are required per stance break
Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or parried
strat: Use the Black Knife Tiche Ash Summons
60-70% damage negation should make most attacks survivable with 40 VIG.
Focus on holy damage negation more than physical, since his melee attacks are easier to avoid.

Particularly affected by offensive Godskin Incanatations, therefore Black Flame Blade, or other offensive Godskin incantations. He has 0 resistance to fire-based attacks and Black Flame incantations deal additional percentage-based damage over time.
Fire weapons are advisable, Magma Blade and the Blasphemous Blade are strong choices. With both weapon arts dealing high fire damage.

Radagon is vulnerable to stance damage, which can break his stance up to three times during the fight. This provides opportunities to reapply buffs, drink flasks, or deal more damage. Weapons with quick guard counters, like Dragon King's Cragblade, are effective here. Slower weapons, like Bloodhound's Fang, may struggle to capitalize on his openings. Most of his attacks have long recovery times, allowing you to use a jumping heavy attack or charged attack.
Use Godskin magic, such as Black Flame Blade, since Godskin Apostle Incantations were designed to defeat gods like Radagon.

The primary melee threat is Radagon's grab. When his arm glows, he prepares a lunging grab with a generous hitbox and limited tracking. This move can kill from full health with 50 Vigor, even with Lionel's Set and damage reduction talismans. To avoid it, start sprinting as soon as he begins his grab, or roll into him to dodge reliably.

Recommended talismans for melee users are Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman, Haligdrake Talisman, and Green Turtle Talisman. This setup will minimize chip damage from his attacks. Radagon’s backswing can still hit you even if you roll past him, so maintain high HP and stamina to exploit his openings. The Crimson Seed Talisman will extend the effectiveness of each flask in this demanding final boss battle.

When fighting Radagon at range, there are two major threats - maybe three. The first is his big ground slam. This is easily identified by him leaping into the air and hovering for a bit. Reflexes say dodge when this hits the ground but that is the last thing you want to do. It's not so much a typical AoE attack as it is a nova. So, the attack spreads out. You want to dodge after he hits. It might take a try or two to get this one figured out. The second major one is when he charges up his hammer and slams it three ...

One note about the first slam is that it might feel like a good time to get in some damage, and it is, but don't get caught with your pants down and in a big animation. Even if he looks like he might attack a spirit or friend, he has a tendency to change targets while up in the air and gives little warning!
The third major thing to watch out for is his lightning bolt. However, this one doesn't have much in the way of trickery, but getting the timing down might take a try or two.

Once you can reliably avoid these three things the rest of it is pretty easy in terms of defense. The biggest trouble is finding the time to get the hits in. Something with a quick animation is your friend, but he is also prone to losing/switching aggro so you can hit him with something big here and there. He also seems to maintain a fairly steady tempo, so his wind-up/wind-down/recovery between attacks feels consistent and can help you get an idea for when to attack.

As for what he is weak to? Good question! Testing would be required, but he seems to take a lot of damage from most things. Glintstone Icecrag hits him really hard, and Stars of Ruin can do some work if you need a bit more range. Hitting him with Ranni's Dark Moon when he loses aggro can give you a little boost in damage going forward thanks to its magic resistance reduction. Quite frankly, he takes a lot of damage and could even be considered fairly squishy, but he has a tendency to take you out of the fight ...

One thing I did find is that Black Knife Tiche (bless her soul) is as good against him she is against most bosses. Her rot-blade or whatever nonsense she flings around can easily take 20% of his Hp by the time its DoT runs out, so she is a good one to use. She's also durable enough that she will last through both fights without issue.

With a little luck and some good timing, you can eliminate Radagon inside a minute, if not quicker, leaving you with just the follow-up fight to deal with. As a sorcerer, that one feels like a lot bigger threat!

For incantation users, Black Flame and Lightning Spear are both effective punishers. Radagon also seems to be vulnerable to the Frenzied Flame spells. Frenzied Burst is highly recommended due to it's long range. For the second phase against Elden Beast, Pest Threads (at close range) deals heavy damage to large targets such as the Beast.

Elden Remembrance.title: Elden Remembrance
intro: Elden Remembrance is a Consumable Item in Elden Ring. Most Consumables grant various effects such as restorative properties for recovering HP, removing certain negative status effects or applying temporary buffs and debuffs, while others can be thrown at enemies to deal damage.
where: Obtained as a reward for defeating the Elden Beast at the Elden Throne.

Scadutree Fragment.title: Scadutree Fragment
intro: Scadutree Fragment is an Upgrade Material in Elden Ring, debuting in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. Scadutree Fragments are optional consumables that can be used to simultaneously enhance offensive and defensive capabilities at any Sites of Grace, acting like a permanent boost to your damage dealt and damage negation in the Land of Shadow.

Sharpshot Talisman.title: Sharpshot Talisman
intro: Sharpshot Talisman is a Talisman in Elden Ring. It is a brand-new Talisman in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. Sharpshot Talisman boosts attack power of precision-aimed shots. Players can use Talismans in Elden Ring to boost a variety of Stats.
where: Where to find Sharpshot Talisman:
Found inside Albinauric's Shack in Scaduview. Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree Interactive Map

Remembrance of the Shadow Sunflower.title: Remembrance of the Shadow Sunflower
intro: Remembrance of the Shadow Sunflower is a Consumable Item in Elden Ring. It is a brand-new Remembrance in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. Most Consumables grant various effects such as restorative properties for recovering HP, removing certain negative status effects or applying temporary buffs and debuffs, while others can be thrown at enemies to deal damage.
where: Dropped from the Scadutree Avatar boss in the Scadutree Base area. [Shadow of the Erdtree ]

Scadutree Avatar.title: Scadutree Avatar
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
Drops 260,000, Remembrance of the Shadow Sunflower, Miquella's Great Rune
strat: Recommended summons: Omenkiller Rollo, Bigmouth Imp, Fire Knight Hilde
Recommended armaments: Fire Knight Greatsword, Mohgwyn's Sacred Spear, Spear of the Impaler
Recommended spells: Frenzied Burst, Flame Fall Upon Them, Pest Threads
Recommended talismans: Godfrey Icon, Fire Scorpion Charm, Dragoncrest Greatshield
Bring Stanching Boluses, Holyproof Dried Liver
Other options include Opaline Hardtear or Bubbletear to lower damage, especially in the third phase where the explosions deal immense damage.
Phase 1

In Phase 1, the Avatar is easy to handle. The battle begins with its triple tree root ranged attack, where it sends out two spiked roots toward you upon entering the Scadutree Base. Dodge these roots and close the distance to deliver heavy attacks to its head. The second spiked root will arrive a bit later than the first one, so you should be mindful of dodging it. If you can get close to the Scadutree Avatar after this attack, you can attack its head to deal a lot of damage.

This boss will continue the phase with one of its basic combos. It will start with the quick left overhead attack, a slightly delayed right overhead attack, and another left overhead. Then, it will pause for a bit, do a delayed right overhead attack, and bury it onto the ground. After a short delay, the ground will explode in the area around it. To dodge this attack your move pattern will go like this:
Dodge roll to your right
Wait for the pause. roll again to the right, then roll right again
Roll as the delayed attack hits the ground, then roll forward (slightly to the right) as the ground explodes

When this attack is dodged properly, you can retaliate with a heavy attack at the end. Throughout this phase, the Avatar will occasionally raise its head and swing at you multiple times. It can do the Sunflower Head Slam, Sunflower Head Charge, and the Sunflower Head Grab. Be ready to back up and evade these swings. These are the basic moves of the Scadutree Avatar and you can dodge them once you get the timing right. Another move is 360 Sweeps and Swing attacks. This is a move where you see the boss spin in a ...

For the special move in Phase 1, it will do the Area of Thorns, where it summons thorns in a large area. This move is quickly followed by the Land of Shadow attack where you see its head glow bright gold and it will cock its head backwards. The sunflower appears to gather like a holy light on its head, and after a short charge, it will explode, creating orbs of holy magic. These orbs will be launched as projectiles that can track your movement. These projectiles can be dodged by sprinting sideways (either left or ...

The first phase is slow-paced, allowing you to predict and learn its attack patterns. Once you deplete its health, the Scadutree Avatar will collapse, only to resurrect a few seconds later with 100% (75%, if it is finished by a riposte) health, marking the start of Phase 2.
Phase 2

Phase 2 introduces a more aggressive and faster Scadutree Avatar. It retains all its previous attacks and adds a powerful thrust move. Upon resurrection, it will immediately charge at you regardless of distance. It will do this 3 times consistently and you need to time your rolls precisely to avoid this attack. Adapt to its increased speed by counter-attacking after each move it makes. If the boss ends up at a long distance, it will do either the long-branch attack or the Land of the Shadow projectile attack.

The key is to stay close, dodge its attacks, and strike its head when it is down. In this phase, you will now see the boss doing a single overhead attack, but it will now conjure thorns at the end of its arm. Even the 360 Swing and Sweep attack will now get a follow-up move, where it will do the same overhead attack that creates thorns at the end. The timing for the dodge roll is still the same during this phase. The Scadutree Avatar will often leave its head exposed after an attack, giving you opportunities to ...
Phase 3

Phase 3 is the most difficult stage of the fight. The Scadutree Avatar retains all attacks from the previous phases and introduces the devastating Charged Light Explosion. This attack is its most powerful one, capable of either one-shotting you or draining 80% of your health upon impact. This attack consists of a long charge time and once it explodes, it will shoot out laser projectiles (javelin-like) that can reach you anywhere in the arena. One way to dodge this is first, you need to get the timing right for ...

As you are nearing the end of this fight, this boss can resolve to do the Charged Light Explosion multiple times, up to three consecutive explosions. At this point, you need to get the timing correct so you can dodge it properly. If you're having difficulty dodging this move, you can try sprinting away and rolling backward, however, doing it this way will not let you get many free hits once it slumps its head on the ground.

Its overall movements are now very fast, requiring heightened focus and quick reflexes. Watch for the telltale sign of this attack: when its chest becomes stationary and glows yellow. When this happens, run as far as possible and lock onto the foe to predict the explosion beams. Keep dodging this attack while looking for opportunities to land heavy blows on its head.

Sorcery users can negate the entire Land of Shadow attack (the rain of golden projectiles) by casting Eternal Darkness and running back, causing all projectiles to get sucked into the black hole. If you do not run back after casting Eternal Darkness, you will still get hit. Use Comet targeting the head of the boss to deal great damage. Optionally, equip a shield with low requirements such as Carian Knight's Shield and enchant it with Scholar's Shield to negate all damage from attacks, though you will still get ...

Frenzied Flame Incantations are a great choice for Faith users. Frenzied Burst has exceptional range and high damage, especially to the head. Ash of War: Flame of the Redmanes is another decent option.

Miquella's Great Rune.title: Miquella's Great Rune

where: Dropped as a reward for defeating the Scadutree Avatar located at Scadutree Base. Scadutree Base is located East of Albinauric's Shack and Northeast of Shadow Keep. See the Scadutree Avatar on the [Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree Map]

Gaius's Greaves is part of the Gaius's Set, and are the greaves of one of the Bosses of the game, Commander Gaius. Gaius's Greaves protect both of the player's legs and feet by applying various defensive properties. They also change the appearance as well when it is equipped. Some armor pieces may be available to both genders, but may be slightly different for male and female characters.
where: The Gaius's Greaves Leg Armor can be found at:
Albinauric's Shack. Dropped by an Albinauric Archer riding a wolf. The rider grants +6381 Runes and the wolf +5490. See Shadow of the Erdtree Map

Dropped by the Fallingstar Beast, who can be found in the crater in Fingerstone Hill. Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree Map

The Two Fingers have responsibilities include selecting Empyrean candidates to inherit the Elden Ring, furnishing these candidates with shadowbound beasts, and offering wisdom to the Tarnished through Finger Readers. You can find a total of seven Two Fingers throughout the game, the only one found alive is in the Roundtable Hold, interpreted by Enia. There are Two ...

Remembrance of the Wild Boar Rider.title: Remembrance of the Wild Boar Rider
intro: Remembrance of the Wild Boar Rider is a Consumable Item in Elden Ring. It is a brand-new Remembrance in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. Most Consumables grant various effects such as restorative properties for recovering HP, removing certain negative status effects or applying temporary buffs and debuffs, while others can be thrown at enemies to deal damage.
where: Dropped by Commander Gaius at the back of the Shadow Keep. Shadow of the Erdtree Map

Commander Gaius.title: Commander Gaius
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
Damage: Standard, Slash, Strike, Pierce, Magic
Drops 230,000, Remembrance of the Wild Boar Rider
strat: Use the Black Knife Tiche Ash Summons
Opt for a Great Hammer like the Heavy Curved Great Club
Bring Flask of Wondrous Physick (Greenburst Crystal Tear and Opaline Hardtear or Windy Crystal Tear) Item
Use Crucible Feather Talisman to make dodging his charge easier

Commander Gaius rides a giant wild boar that can rush forward in great speed. You will be battling both the rider and the Wild Boar here, and they can combine their attacks as you take them on. For melee users, the key to this fight is heavy attacks and jump attacks. This trades off defense for a chance to break the boss' stance and deal additional damage. While fighting this boss, try to stick to its sides and back. This gives you the best chances to avoid getting damaged especially during the first phase. The ...

To begin, Commander Gaius will always open the fight with the Wild Boar Rush as you enter the arena, which is a move where he charges at you as you enter the arena. You can dodge by rolling into him at the very last second. While you are near this boss, it can use Wild Swing together with a Kick and Head Slam from the wild boar. If you're feeling confident, you can roll towards the swing of the weapon, and toward the Wild Boar for the Head Slam. The kick is a little difficult to dodge because it gives very little ...

The boss' second phase will begin once its health drops to about 50%. You will notice this when the boss clutches its body as the purple color mixed with lightning courses throughout his armor. During this phase, the boss will start using all of its gravity attacks and its basic attacks will deal additional gravity damage. These attacks are easily discernible because his weapon will glow purple, and you can hear a crackling audio cue as it charges up.

There are about 5 Gravity attacks that we saw when we took down this boss, and one of the most dangerous ones is the Gravity Plunge. This is an attack that begins with a jump toward the sky, the boss will spin in place to charge the attack and plunge at high speed. The impact has a pretty wide AoE, so you shouldn't underestimate it. Ideally, you want to roll backward and away from the impact, but in situations where you prefer a high-risk/high-reward scenario, you can try to roll forward as the boss plunges and ...

The other gravity attack worth mentioning is the Gravity Thrust, this is a move that he does where he charges up his weapon with gravity magic and then makes an upward thrust with it, creating an AoE damage within the area around him. When he does this, roll forward to dodge and you can retaliate with a light attack.

Commander Gaius deals primarily physical damage and moderate amounts of magic damage. A greatshield with full physical block and high Guard Boost stats can block every attack Gaius can throw, making him extremely vulnerable to guard-counter loadouts; about 6 guard counters with a katana can cause the first stance break.

Final Tips: Don't forget to consume your Flask of Wondrous Physick and summon Black Knife Tiche at the start. The bonus stamina recovery speed and damage negation will help in this fight. Summoning Black Knife Tiche is only recommended for players who don't require FP in Combat as it consumes 132 FP but will greatly benefit you against Commander Gaius. Alternatively, you may also use Cerulean Hidden Tear in your physick if you don't have the required FP for Black Knife Tiche (this eliminates all FP consumption).

The fight will always start with the boss charging at you. He will dodge all attacks during this first charge. The hitbox for this attack is massive, and a mistimed dodge through the boss will have you take damage from the charge once, twice, or even thrice, likely one-shotting you. Instead, dodge to the side, or use ashes of war such as Bloodhound's Step, Vow of the Indomitable, or Raptor of the Mists. For sorcery users, Miriam's Vanishing can be used similarly to Bloodhound's Step and can evade the attack. This ...

Sorcery users will require spells with good tracking, given Commander Gaius' tremendous speed and maneuverability. Stars of Ruin is perfect in that regard. Carian Slicer is another great option. Avoid spells with long casting times that would leave you open to incoming attacks.
Incantation users should employ the same strategy casting spells such as Catch Flame or Black Flame. If you find the opening, Burn, O Flame! might be another good option.

Remembrance of the Impaler.title: Remembrance of the Impaler
intro: Remembrance of the Impaler is a Consumable Item in Elden Ring. It is a brand-new Remembrance in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. Most Consumables grant various effects such as restorative properties for recovering HP, removing certain negative status effects or applying temporary buffs and debuffs, while others can be thrown at enemies to deal damage.
where: Obtained upon defeating Messmer the Impaler [Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree ]

Messmer the Impaler.title: Messmer the Impaler
facts: Parryable: Yes, but 3 parries are required per stance break
Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or parried
Damage: Standard, Slash, Strike, Pierce, Fire
Drops 400,000, Remembrance of the Impaler, Messmer's Kindling
strat: Recommended summons: Mimic Tear
Recommended armaments: Staff of the Guilty, Bloodfiend's Arm, Great Stars, Reduvia, Rivers of Blood, Heater Shield, Fingerprint Stone Shield (Fire affinity)
Any skill, that lowers the player's position is good to both attack and avoid damage (Messmer mostly go for spear in forward, not down).
Recommended spells: Flame Protect Me, Impenetrable Thorns, Golden Vow, Swarm of Flies, Borealis's Mist
Recommended talismans: Flamedrake Talisman +3, Great-Jar's Arsenal, Lord of Blood's Exultation
Other items: Albinauric Set, Briar Set, Greenspill Crystal Tear, Stonebarb Cracked Tear

For the most part, you will want to stay close to him because of the long reach of his spear and flame spells. When you're fighting Messmer at a close range, you will have more chance of retaliating and chipping away at his health while he recovers. Engaging Messmer patiently is the best strategy to effectively take him down. When he finishes a string of attacks, focus on breaking his poise by pulling off heavy attacks for a chance to deal significant damage.

Due to Messmer's speed, you need to approach him with the right mix of patience and aggressiveness. This boss can quickly transition between offense and defense by quickly disengaging with a leap after he finishes a move. Be aware that Messmer counters swiftly after sustaining damage, too. His speed and precision in combat are his biggest asset, requiring observation of his movements to avoid being overwhelmed.

One of the basic moves that Messmer makes is the Flaming Spear Lunge, this is when you see him leap into the air as he thrusts his weapon and then crash on the ground with his spear engulfed in flames. This movement is dodgeable and will take some time to get used to but you can do this by rolling forward as he thrusts his weapon, waiting for the delay as he prepares to crash, and then rolling forward again to stay close to him. This allows you to attack him while he's recovering.

Next up is Messmer's Flaming Assault, which is a 3-string attack where he combines this move with his flame spells. While the spear is engulfed in flames, he will cast spells with his flaming right hand and he will do the following attacks:
When he swings his right arm, he will use a fire spell that affects the immediate area in front of him
Quick Thrust with the spear, followed by a quick jump to reposition himself and another spear thrust
Flame Spell where he twists in place to swing his spear and creates a flame surrounding him

To dodge this move, you need to learn when he will do this by paying attention to his arm. If you see him cross it over and it's engulfed in flames, he will do this attack. To dodge, roll to the right if you're too close, otherwise, rolling backward is safe enough. You need to dodge as soon as he swings his arm engulfed in flames. For the second part, roll forward as soon as he thrusts with his spear, wait for the delay as he jumps to reposition himself, then dodge as soon as he lands on his new spot. Finally, for ...

Messmer's powerful Grab attack will kill most players instantly. It is important to dodge this attack to avoid an instant death. When Messmer's hand begins glowing, that is the sign he is about to grab you. Once he begins to descend his arm to grab you, roll either to the sides or forward. This will leave an opening to hit him. If you can break his stance, remember to go in front of him and just lightly press R1 (once) to do a light attack. This will do a critical hit and can deal a lot more damage than any ...

The next basic attack combo is a 4-String attack where he throws out a flame spell in close range, followed by 2 quick thrust, and a dash flame 360. To dodge this move, you will roll backward to dodge the flame spell, then wait out a bit, and roll toward him for the quick thrust, wait for the delay here, and roll toward him again for the second quick thrust, and then, roll forward towards him for the 360. This is the recommended move so you can get some free hits while he recovers. There's a variation of this move ...

Finally, one more move that is worth mentioning is the Messmer's Assault which consists of multiple string attacks and usually ends with an explosion at the end. The move will begin with Messmer jumping up with an Airborne Sweep 360, followed by a quick spear swing, an upward thrust to launch himself upwards and end the move with a plunge to create an explosion. This move will create spears exploding from the ground. To dodge this move, you will do the following per string of attack:
Roll to your right back
Roll towards him to be point blank or back to mitigate damage
Roll towards him
Again, roll towards than him and punish/heal, since recovery is long
There's also a variation of this move called Airborne Sweeps Combo, which is more manageable to dodge.

As the battle goes on and Messmer's health reaches the halfway mark, the fight stops. The fight pauses and a cutscene shows Messmer kneeling and performing a ritualistic act, removing one of his own eyes and shattering it, causing the area to glow red. This indicates the beginning of Phase 2.

The battle begins with the Serpent Explosive Bite which is where he turns into a big serpent with Scarlet Rot crawling on its skin. The Serpent bites down on the ground and as the fang hits, the ground beneath it will explode. Then, Messmer will revert to his humanoid form. While in this state, he executes his attacks with increased speed compared to his previous form, making him a more powerful boss.

Turn immediately left, just before the large fingercreeper lying in wait, and head east between the two finger statues. After a short drop down, keep to the left of ...

intro: Revered Spirit Ash is an Upgrade Material in Elden Ring, debuting in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. These special items are optional Upgrade Materials that can be used at any Sites of Grace to boost summoned spirits and the spectral steed's abilities to deal and negate damage.

Letter for Freyja.title: Letter for Freyja
intro: Letter for Freyja is a Key Item in Elden Ring. It is a Key Item found in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. Rugalea the Great Red Bear.title: Rugalea the Great Red Bear
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
strat: Use the ?? Ash Summons
Use the ?? Spell
Bring Sleep Pot, Eternal Sleep Pot
Rugalea the Great Red Bear is a boss that can spawn with "Golden Eyes" and makes it drop 5x more Runes (over 1,500,000). This effect is random.

Rugalea only has a few attacks, with one having another variant. Rugalea has a Single-fist Ground Burst and a Double-Fist Ground burst. During this move, the boss will dig one or both claws into the ground and throw rocks in your direction as it lifts its paws upward. This attack can be indicated when it readies one claw or both claws to dig into the ground. This attack creates an AoE that affects the area around it, and so the recommended way to avoid this attack is to dodge to either side.

Another claw attack it does is its Slashes, it will rise up and swing both its claws at you one at a time, this attack can be indicated when Rugalea stands up on its hind legs and pulls its forelegs back before attacking. You can dodge back with each swing to avoid this attack.

This boss has 2 other attacks, one of which is its Body slam. This is where Rugalea rises up and slams down on its belly. This attack can be indicated when Rugalea rises up, and lands on its front paws briefly after. You can dodge back or to the sides to avoid this attack.

The last attack Rugalea has is its Mighty Roar, it will stand on its back legs and let out a mighty roar that knocks you down. When you see Rugalea rise on its back legs and not go back down, you will need to dodge by rolling forward and get behind it to avoid the attack.
When Rugalea the Great Red Bear is defeated, it will drop 210,000 Runes and the Roar of Rugalea.

facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken
Damage: Slash, Strike (all Hippos), Pierce, Holy (Golden Hippopotamus only)
Drops 200,000, Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns, Scadutree Fragment x2
strat: Recommended Summons: Mimic Tear, Black Knife Tiche Ashes
Recommended armaments: Blasphemous Blade
Recommended Skills: Lion's Claw, Savage Lion's Claw
Bring ?? Item

Aside from the aggressive bites, this boss will also slam its head which can throw you off balance and because of the size of this boss, it is better to dodge toward its body and away from the head. This creates more distance from the head compared to rolling backward. The Golden Hippopotamus is weak to heavy attacks, and you need to keep an eye out for openings. The boss takes a few seconds of rest after it finishes a move. If you happen to break its poise, be patient and walk towards the head, and press R1 to ...

This boss can also do the Belly Slam attack where you see it stand on its legs. This move has a long wind-up time and a slight delay before it slams its belly. For this move, the best way to dodge is to roll on either side, and you will be able to retaliate with an attack directly on its head. When the boss' health drops to 50%, it will create golden quills on its head and body. One of the changes that this will make is that, whenever the boss does the Belly Slam, its quills will rain from above. This will affect ...

Lastly, one of the moves is the Golden Quill Air Strike which will rain down golden quills, or combine them with a spinning 360 attack. This move can be dodged by rolling twice backward in quick succession. The boss might follow up this move with another combo so make sure to pay attention to its next movements before you commit to doing any attacks after.
The same applies to incantation users, who can cast Pest Threads to similar effect. If you find the opening, Burn, O Flame! is also a great option.

The Blasphemous Blade is extremely useful for this fight. The boss is already weak to fire, and the weapon's unique skill has a chance to hit twice due to its size, which will provide extra healing.

When engaging the Divine Beast Dancing Lion, it is important to focus on the movements of its head, as this shows signs of its attacks. By closely observing its head, you can anticipate its next attack and prepare for it. This is especially useful when dodging its Grab Attack and other moves. The best moment to strike is right after the beast finishes its string of attack. It usually recovers after it finishes a move and gives you time to strike back if you're within striking distance.

The common opening attack of this boss is the Lunge Attack where you see the boss jump high, and do a lunge attack to crash on the ground towards you. Then, it will follow up the move with a backflip kick. You can avoid this attack by slightly moving towards your left as the boss lands nearby, wait for a brief moment, and do a forward dodge roll as you see it kick off the ground doing the backflip. You can go in with a heavy attack if dodged properly, or do several light hits. This move is usually followed up by a ...

Another combo that this boss can do is the 360 Combo where it starts with 2 quick bites in succession and ends with a delayed tail whip. The timing for this is similar to the 3-Hit Combo, but you have to watch out for the incoming tail whip. You can stay close to the boss as he does the 2 quick bites, and then roll forward for the tail whip as it comes around.

When you're far away from the boss, this beast can utilize moves like Leaping Bite where it will sprint for a bit and leap through the air towards you, attacking you with a bite. This attack can be dodged by blocking it if you have a shield or rolling to the left to evade the attack. On the other hand, when you're fighting this boss up close, it will do the Spinning Whirlwind by spinning from its position and start blowing a lot of heavy winds, almost acting like a tornado. When hit, this attack will break your ...

This boss can also do a Grab Attack where you will see it gnash its mouth twice before it lunges forward to try and grab you. To dodge this move, roll forward as the head closes in. If it hits, you will be grabbed, but like many other grabs, you can reduce the damage taken by mashing the light attack and block buttons. If you survive this grab, you will receive a negative effect that will heal the boss the next time you use a Flask of Crimson Tears. The amount healed depends on the upgrade level of your flask; a ...

Consistent heavy blows can break the Divine Beast Dancing Lion's stance, leaving its head vulnerable. When this happens, do a series of melee attacks to damage and deplete its health. Be prepared for its recovery, as the creature will often counter with a ground smash and use its moving whirlwind attack to create distance while doing damage.

Upon reaching 70% health, the Divine Beast Dancing Lion will leap into the air and enter Phase 2. The Dancing Lion will always start Phase 2 by switching to the Lightning Phase. It is important to note that there is no pattern in which element the boss will use next, as its order will be random. While the elements of its attacks change in each phase, the base attack patterns remain the same from the beginning, with additional elements. For the Dancing Lion's lightning attacks, stay away from the lightning pools ...

The strategy from here is simple - keep your distance and use quick but effective spells like Comet. While Freyja and Tiche are keeping the Divine Beast busy you should be able to do some solid damage from a distance. If the Divine Beast turns its attention to you, dodge, heal, and do what you need to do until your counterpart(s) can help take aggro.You will know you’ve entered phase two when the divine beast starts using its lightning attacks around 70% health. These attacks have a large AOE and can do some real ...
With help from your summons, this battle shouldn’t drag out terribly long. The boss is weak to Rotten Breath and Swarm of Flies.
