When fighting her as a melee character, focus on her central human body as well as her centipede fangs and scorpion stinger, which act as her arms. These parts move independently, allowing her to launch multiple simultaneous attacks, such as swinging her spear while her stinger strikes from another direction. Her attacks include Heavy Spear Thrusts, Sweeping Stinger strikes, and Biting Fangs.

Romina’s common opening move is the Centipede Sweep, where her centipede body swings from right to left. You can dodge this by rolling forward just before it hits. This allows you to get close and deliver a full heavy attack. Be aware that she may follow up with a Quick Dash to reposition and swing her poleblade. This can be avoided by rolling to your left or backward.

Stay as close as possible to Romina, as some of her sweep attacks won't hit you at point-blank range. Being near her also makes her attack pattern more predictable. For instance, after her usual opening attack, closing the distance with a dodge roll will cause her follow-up attack to miss if you are right beside her.

One thing that you should do is to always look at her Poleblade, when you see it glowing red, this means that the weapon is enchanted with Scarlet Rot. If this weapon hits you while the enchantment is active, it will cause Scarlet Rot build-up. So always be wary of her weapon status. One of the combos that she does with her enchanted weapon, is the Leap Combo where she starts with a poleblade sweep, an overhead attack, and then she jumps high in the air, and then plunges her weapon down. To dodge this move you ...
Roll to your left for the sweep attack
Roll forward (slightly to your right) as she swings the overhead attack
Pause here and pay attention when her weapon flashes pink for a brief moment, then roll forward at that exact moment

When this move is dodged properly, you can get a couple of free hits as she recovers. This move also has a variation where she would skip the 3rd part of the attack and will just do an enchanted weapon combo. She also has another basic move where she makes 3 quick sweeping movements with her poleblade without enchantments. Then finally, she can also do the Rolling Attack where Romina will curl up into a ball, and then roll around the arena. After she is done rolling, she will then slam the ground and do a swing ...

After she finishes a combo, quickly counterattack to take advantage of the brief windows of vulnerability. Her attacks, while powerful, have high recovery times, allowing you to dodge and immediately counter. When she begins a combo, dodge her attacks by rolling to the side or towards her to close the distance. Immediately after dodging, counter with heavy attacks to break her poise. Frequent usage of jumping and heavy attacks is recommended as it can stagger her, leaving her open to further attacks.

One of her special moves is the Double Spin 360 Combo. This is a move where you see her lift her human body up as her weapon glows red, then, she will do 2 full spins while swinging her poleblade. Then, she pauses after this move to recover. This move can be dodged by rolling to the left, then dodging to the left again after a slight delay. This move usually causes Romina to end up at a far position from you, but she will take time to recover and you can do at least 1 light attack or a jump attack if you sprint up ...

During Phase 2, her attacks remain the same but she can now conjure butterflies that will explode after a short period. She will transition into the 2nd Phase when her health drops to 50%, and you will see her surround herself with pink lighting with butterflies circling her. After a brief period, this will cause a whirlwind in the small area, then she follows up this move with more butterflies in the outer area of the whirlwind that will explode randomly throughout the arena. To dodge the Butterfly Bombs move, ...

Incantations have a lot of options, as the boss is weak to lightning, holy, and frost. Knight's Lightning Spear is a good choice, as the follow-up spears can usually still hit even if the main spear misses. Pest-Thread Spears have high tracking and damage. Romina is weak to Swarm of Flies.

One of the best options among Sorceries is Roiling Magma. Buff it with Talisman of the Dread, cast with Gelmir Glintstone Staff or have it in the off-hand. Upon entry to the arena throw the Hefty Oil Pot. Considering your catalyst's sorcery scaling is maxed out, first cast should take most part of the boss's HP. Impenetrable Thorns is also an excellent choice.
Spirit Ash summons and the NPC furled finger Dryleaf Dane will be a great help to ranged users.

Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers.title: Count Ymir Mother of Fingers
facts: Does not carry a Flask of Crimson Tears
Is vulnerable to a backstab critical
Armor: High Priest Hat, High Priest Robe, High Priest Gloves, High Priest Undergarments
Drops 210,000, Ymir's Bell Bearing, Maternal Staff, High Priest Set
strat: Use spells that do Lightning damage, such as Lightning Spear
Equip fast-hitting weapon types, such as Hand-to-Hand Arts and Fists
Use weapons or spells that deal Fire Damage to quickly deal with the summoned Fingercreepers.

Count Ymir has several sorceries up his sleeve, including Cherishing Fingers, this is where he lifts his staff and slams it back down to cast a ring of six fingers that surround him, this attack can be indicated when Count Ymir raises and slams his staff down directly. When the fingers come up, it will deal damage to you so you will need to dodge backward and attack his once the fingers go away.

Another one is Glintstone Nails, in which Count Ymir will lift up his staff once again but wave it around to launch six tracking projectiles towards you. You can easily avoid this attack by simply sidestepping or perfectly timing your forward dodge roll to avoid the projectiles. You can also use the pillars around the area if you are having difficulties with dodging this attack.

His last attack is Finger Spawn. Just like Metyr, he can also summon Fingercreepers, though the move is slow and it leaves him open to attack. Ymir will stay stationary while summoning. He will start groaning, and dark green liquid can be seen as Fingercreepers move out of his body. Just like for the Metyr boss fight, you can take those out first, so you won't be overwhelmed.
Once Count Ymiris defeated, he will drop Ymir's Bell Bearing, the Maternal Staff, and the High Priest Set.

For Faith builds, Frenzied Burst can reach all the way across the arena. You can just stand at the opposite end of the cathedral from Ymir and blast away, he will usually just stay over there. The Fire Damage will also kill the Fingercreepers quickly. If you're feeling risky, Inescapable Frenzy can be used, though he is rather resistant to Madness.

For Intelligence builds, Stars of Ruin or Star Shower can keep him on the defensive. Use attacks like Carian Greatsword or Adula's Moonblade to deal with the adds. Carian Piercer can easily roll-catch Ymir and knock him down.

For ranged users, consider using Fire Arrows or Explosive Bolts to deal with the Fingercreepers. Otherwise, be wary of his Cherishing Fingers deflecting any of your projectiles. Rancor Shot with the Bone Bow or Enchanted Shot can land some hits from afar.

As Red Bear approaches, be ready to anticipate its attacks. One of its most common moves is the Two-Claw combo, where it slashes from left to right. As the fight progresses, this combo adapts into a four-hit sequence, adding upward and downward slashes. Its most powerful attack is the Bear Roar, where it takes out the head of Ralva the Great Red Bear, causing high damage in a wide area twice. This attack is dangerous, so keep your distance when you see it being prepared.

The key to defeating Red Bear is to match its agility and time your attacks perfectly. After each combo, Red Bear pauses for a split second, providing a brief window for you to counterattack. Use this opportunity to land a few hits before retreating. A good strategy is to lure Red Bear towards you, letting it chase you until you are within range to attack quickly. This tactic often breaks its poise, allowing you to deliver multiple attacks. However, remain observant and cautious, as Red Bear can counter your ...

Chief Bloodfiend.title: Chief Bloodfiend
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or parried
strat: Recommended Spirit Ashes: Black Knife Tiche
Recommended Armaments: Black Knife
Recommended Ashes of War: Bloodhound's Step
Recommended Spells: Rotten Breath
Other items: Cerulean Hidden Tear, Opaline Bubbletear, Opaline Hardtear, Windy Crystal Tear, Stanching Boluses (to alleviate Blood Loss effect)

Each of its attacks results in a long recovery period, providing opportunities to counterattack after every move the boss makes. The worry during this fight is its jumping attacks, which cover a wide damage area and can be difficult to avoid if you miss your timing. The Chief Bloodfiend can also inflict Hemorrhage through skills and attacks, but luckily, this boss is weak against Poison, Scarlet Rot, and Frostbite.

At the start of the battle, the Chief Bloodfiend opens the fight with a Plunge Attack where he lands towards you. Then, this is followed closely by 3 Quick Swing Attacks and finishes it off with a delayed swing. Be prepared to roll to the left to evade this opening attack, then do another roll to the left. While you're on this side, you are free to run back toward it and then roll forward for the last delayed swing. Once you've dodged, move in quickly to land a few hits before retreating to a safe distance.

Another move that this boss will make is the Triple Ground Stomp where the boss will stomp the ground for 2 quick steps, and end it with one delayed stomp. To dodge this move, roll to the left in quick succession, and then watch out for the third (delayed) stomp. You can roll forward right before the foot hits the ground so you can get some free hits on the boss. This pattern of dodging and countering is key to reading the Bloodfiend's attacks. Given the boss's slow recovery times, you can take advantage of these ...

As the fight goes on, this boss will also pull off moves like Ground Slam attack where the boss jumps up high in the air and crashes on top of you. This can also be combined with a delayed Club Smash. When he's making this move, you will see him raise both hands in the air while clutching the club, and it opens its mouth right before he swings it. The moves are pretty standard and the timing for dodges is as expected.

Overall, the boss gives a simple sequence, and timing your moves correctly will allow you to chip away at the Bloodfiend's health. Always be alert for its stomping attacks and be ready to dodge. By maintaining this rhythm of evasion and counterattack, you'll find that the Chief Bloodfiend, despite its power, is a manageable boss.

The key to defeating Dryleaf Dane lies in timing your attacks to stagger him. His poise is relatively weak, allowing you to break it easily and attack him while he’s down. Be particularly wary of his jumping attacks; these can be countered effectively by attacking him mid-air. Successfully doing so will stun him, providing you with ample time to land additional hits.

During the fight, focus on maintaining a balance between offense and defense. Wait for openings in his attacks to strike, and capitalize on his recovery periods. By staggering Dryleaf Dane and countering his jumps, you can reduce his health fast and emerge victorious in this challenging mini-boss.
Also, you can use weapon types with high Poise damage such as greatswords to ignore all of his attacks. You can keep spamming attacks until Dryleaf Dane is defeated, as you can easily stagger him.

Rakshasa.title: Rakshasa
facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being parried
Is vulnerable to a backstab critical
Armor: Rakshasa Helm, Rakshasa Armor, Rakshasa Gauntlets, Rakshasa Greaves
Drops 90,000, Rakshasa's Great Katana, Rakshasa's Set
strat: Recommended Ashes of War: Flame of the Redmanes
Recommended skills: Golden Crux, Taker's Flames, Wave of Gold
Recommended skills: Dragonmaw
Recommended talismans: Fire Scorpion Charm, Ritual Sword Talisman, Shard of Alexander
Recommended armaments: Any shield for Parry
Other items: Flame-Shrouding Cracked Tear, Opaline Hardtear, Opaline Bubbletear

When Rakshasa prepares to slash, she often backs up slightly before executing the attack. This gives you a brief moment to anticipate and dodge. Additionally, when she jumps into the air to perform Leaping Slash, you can usually counter this move by attacking her mid-air. This tactic can interrupt his attack and give you an advantage.

During close-range combat, it’s crucial to retreat occasionally and adapt a defensive stance. Rakshasa can almost always counter with her own attacks unless you stagger her first. Keeping a balance between offense and defense is key. Make sure to land your hits when you see an opening but be ready to dodge and retreat to avoid her counterattacks. She can do the Double Slash move where she makes a double slash with her katana to damage you. You can counter this by rolling to the left or right to evade. ...

Watch her movements closely, anticipate her attacks, and strike when the moment is right. By maintaining a balance between aggression and defense, you can overcome this boss. Rakshasa has hyper armor during all of her attacks, making it impossible to stagger with light attacks. This makes her kind of a difficult boss to deal with, as the window to attack her are pretty tight due to her having a fast attack interval.

If your build can use a shield, I would recommend using it so you could go for parries as all of her attacks can be parried except for the Leaping Slash. Parrying Rakshasa will make the boss fight trivial, as you can continuously keep parrying her and doing Critical Damage to her.
Make use of spells with tracking or that can otherwise overcome her input reading. Such spells include Pest-Thread Spears and Night Comet.

Promised Consort Radahn.title: Promised Consort Radahn
facts: Parryable: Yes, but 3 parries are required per stance break
Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or parried
Damage: Standard, Pierce, Magic, Fire, (phase 1) Standard, Pierce, Magic, Fire, Holy (phase 2)
Phase 2 begins as soon as Radahn goes below 65% HP
Drops 500,000, Remembrance of a God and a Lord
strat: As the final boss of Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree, Promised Consort Radahn is unanimously the hardest boss of the DLC, and one of the hardest bosses in the entire game, considered to be similar in difficulty to Malenia. Similar to Godfrey, the fight is designed for the player to constantly be up close, dodging Radahn's heavy hitting sword slashes and signature gravity magic while finding opportunities in between his combos to heal or deal damage, with one greed hit potentially costing the player the attempt ...
The Best Tips for Promised Consort Radahn:
Recommended Scadutree Blessing: 18 is a minimum (20 is suggested)
Recommended buffs — Golden Vow (both phases), Black Flame's Protection (phase 1), Divine Fortification/Lord's Divine Fortification (phase 2)

If you have completed Thiollier and Ansbach's questlines, you may summon them to assist you in this fight. While they do offer support, status buildup, and can alleviate aggro for a time, summons are not recommended for this fight (and required to complete questline), as they notably increase Radahn's healthbar (and resistances to status buildup).
Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman — physical damage mitigation
Golden Braid — holy damage mitigation for second phase
Two-Headed Turtle Talisman - stamina regeneration
Dagger Talisman (Parry/Riposte type build)
Curved Sword Talisman - Guard-counter build
Greatshield Talisman - Guard-counter build/Shield-type build
Beloved Stardust is not recommended, as while it grants shorter cast time it lowers damage negation by 30%
Outside Lion's Claw, any skill that deals Pierce Damage is recommended for this fight (e.g. Giant Hunt)
Spear Talisman - Tank build paired with pierce-type weapon
Two-Handed Sword Talisman - Strength builds
Verdigris Discus - Tank build
Offensive — Thorny Cracked Tear (physical), Tear appropriate for main damage type inflicted by player (elemental)
Defensive — Opaline Hardtear or Opaline Bubbletear
Radahn's Great Rune - 15% more HP, Stamina, and FP
Morgott's Great Rune - 25% more HP
Miquella's Great Rune (tool) - Removes charmed effect from first grab attack. It is recommended to defeat Scadutree Avatar before this boss to acquire this item.

Hefty Rot Pot - Can quickly inflict Scarlet Rot and drain 30% HP over 90 seconds. Only one pot is needed in phase 1 and can be thrown after the Gravity Rush. In phase 2 you will need two pots (three in in NG+3), and they can be thrown during the Light of Miquella charge-up if you are willing to tank the damage. Ingredients for pots can be farmed.
Boiled Crab - Alternative source of physical defense if you lack the faith needed for the recommended buffs above

Since Radahn often starts the battle with a gap-closing Gravity Rush, it's recommended to apply buffs before entering the arena. Once you do enter, you will have just enough time for two short actions (summoning, flasks, etc) before you need to dodge. Gravity Rush is fairly easy to dodge by rolling into it at the last second, which will leave you an opportunity punish with a heavy attack.

Rellana Twin Moon Knight.title: Rellana Twin Moon Knight
facts: Parryable: Yes, but 2 parries are required per stance break
Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or parried
Damage: Standard, Slash, Pierce, Magic, Fire
Drops 240,000, Remembrance of the Twin Moon Knight
strat: Rellana is one of the hardest bosses that you will encounter in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree, with a particular focus on brutal boss design. She combines swift and aggressive melee attacks, often with short reaction time, with ranged magic spells to form a very deadly arsenal for both new and veteran players. Once she enters Phase 2, her combo attacks deal extra magic and fire damage, she gets new, optional extensions to her combo strings, and can add addtional attacks to final blows, allowing her to deal ...
The Best Tips for Rellana, Twin Moon Knight:
Recommended Spirit Ashes: Greatshield Soldiers, Black Knife Tiche, Mimic Tear, Black Knight Commander Andreas
Recommended Ash of War: Flame of the Redmanes, Giant Hunt, Wing Stance
Recommended Spells: Rotten Breath, Swarm of Flies, Lightning Spear, Barrier of Gold
Also recommended to craft Spellproof Dried/Pickled Liver.
There is a pool of water in the center of arena, so it's recommended to bring some weapons that can deal Lightning Damage.

The boss's long variable combos make it difficult to get near her to launch your attack, but the player should particularly observe her 'Forward Thrust Combos', as they often provide the best punish windows.:
3-string attack combo: she slices each weapon once and ends with Double Thrust with both light greatswords.
6-string attack combo: she starts with an upward Thrust with each weapon, followed by one spinning attack, a quick thrust with each weapon, and ends with another Double Thrust.

The key to determining the end of her attack patterns is when she does the move slow. If it's fast, there's a big chance that it will be followed up by a slow attack, then if it's slow (or heavy) then, you can go in for an attack as she recovers.
When you see an opening, opt for a heavy attack for a chance to stagger her.

The second phase of the fight begins when her health drops below 50%. Rellana will infuse her Greatswords with Glintstone and Flame elements. The greatswords will glow blue and orange. The boss becomes more dangerous and the moves become more difficult to dodge. The dodge frames become shorter and the AoE of skills become larger.

Fire. The flame element creates the widest AoE when using the Sleight of Sword - Fire. This also creates smaller rings of fire in the outer AoE but they don't deal as much damage in the center of the skill. Ideally, you can roll backward three times to get yourself out of the area. Make sure to pay attention to the outer rings as you run to safety.

Magic. When you see her cast the huge Magical Greatsword, be prepared for the first downward vertical slash, this is immediately followed by a giant horizontal spin slash that reaches nearly the entire room. Make sure to dodge early for this attack because it has a deceptively wide reach. Roll forward to get a free hit on her if you get the timing right.

Another spell that she can use is the Glintblade Slicer that she uses when you're far away from her. This is an attack where she swings her weapon downward and sends a blue arc that tracks your movements. The arc varies in position, others are vertical, horizontal, or slanted. To dodge the Glintblade Slicer, you can run away to the left for the first two (if you're far enough), then dodge roll twice for the 3rd and 4th slicer, and then, go for a forward roll for the 5th one. This will allow you to close the gap.

After a while, this boss will use Twin Moons, which protects them from incoming damage and is closely followed by a plunge attack. If you get hit by the falling moon, you will get stunned and you will not be able to roll away to avoid further damage. The Pearldrake Talisman will reduce incoming Elemental Damage. Sometimes she will use Twin Moons at at close range or she will jump away to execute it. The distance will not make much of a change since you still need to jump or dodge roll (any direction) at the exact ...
As the fight comes to an end, the boss will alternate between Physical and Elemental Attacks. Always pay attention to her light greatswords, because this will tell you what her next move is.

Incantation users can make use of tanky spirit ash summons to keep Rellana still. Meanwhile, the summoner can cast rot breath and swarm of flies from a distance. The goal is to defeat her quickly, before she uses the more damaging abilities in her second phase. It is possible to defeat her before she summons the twin moons. If she does summon them, remember to jump three times (a third time when she lands).

When the fight begins, the Ghostflame Dragon will likely start with a Ghostflame Breath attack, which does frostbite damage. Watch for the dragon to wave its head downward as a sign that it’s about to unleash this attack. Due to its slow movements, this attack is relatively easy to predict and avoid. Use your Greatshield to block physical attacks, but rely on your agility to dodge its more powerful attacks. If you're not using a shield, you can roll in either direction (left or right).

The dragon’s legs are its weakest points, so prioritize attacking them whenever you see an opening. Stay close to its legs to minimize the risk of being hit by its more powerful attacks. Be observant of its movements and when the dragon raises its legs, back up and move out of the way to avoid being stomped. The dragon will also perform a ground smash after taking flight, so be prepared to dodge this attack as well. When you see the dragon's head, you can also try to do a jump attack if you can to apply an ...

At mid-range, the Ghostflame Dragon will use a Double Chomp attack, thrusting its jaws towards you. This move is also predictable due to the dragon’s slow overall movement. Stay agile and keep your Greatshield ready to block when necessary. At about 50% health, this boss will do a massive Ghostflame AoE attack. You will know this move when you see it stand up and its chest is burning with Ghostflame. To dodge this, keep running in the opposite direction until the animation ends. The AoE size does cover a lot of ...

The Ghostflame Dragon utilizes Ghostflame strikes that can inflict frostbite, so ensure you have remedies for this status effect. Its slow movements make it a mid-difficulty boss, as its attacks are generally easy to read and anticipate. The ultimate key to defeating this dragon is to observe its movements carefully and dodge when needed. Exploit its weak points by attacking its legs, and use your Greatshield strategically to block its physical attacks while remaining agile to avoid the more dangerous moves. ...

facts: Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or parried
strat: Summons: Black Knife Tiche, Mimic Tear, Greatshield Soldier Ashes
Spells: Glintstone Pebble
Bring any Greatshield

While fighting this boss, make sure to keep your target locked on them so they don't sneak up on you. This also lets you be on guard for any of their attacks. Despite their quick movement, their slashes are comparatively slow because of the wind-up. He holds up his weapon for a few frames before launching the attack and lets you predict their next move. You can alternate going offense and defense by holding up your shield when he's attacking, and then attacking him when he pulls back. This should give you a few ...

The boss will begin the fight with a move called Magic Slash. He will teleport midair in front of the player and will slash downward to bring forth magical damage in a small area. You can dodge this attack by rolling backward, or to your right. We recommend the latter to close the gap and land a free heavy attack. There's a short pause after the move that lets you hit him freely and you can cut off the rest of his attack pattern.

Another move that is worth mentioning is the Orb Cuts. He usually does this when you attempt an attack while he's guarding, and you will see him raise his sword above his head and stabs forward to create an orb around him. This generates an energy that cuts anything within the area. Similar to the Waterfowl Dance but, the boss will stay only in one place. This means that you can dodge this attack by rolling backward.

He has about 3 Magic attacks aside from his Standard Sword attacks. The magic ones are deadlier than his attacks, make sure to keep an eye on his sword if it's glowing blue, or white. When you get the chance, attempt to strike him from behind repeatedly to break his poise. With the help of any spirit summons, this fight shouldn't take long.

Use the ?? Spell

NOTE: The Black Knight Edredd boss may spawn with "Golden Eyes" which makes the boss drop x5 Runes (about 400,000) upon defeating it.

At the start of the battle, Edredd starts with the Spinning Soaring Blade Slash. This move involves the knight spotting you from afar and flying towards you while spinning its blades. To avoid taking damage, quickly roll towards Edredd. Successfully evading it provides a brief window to counter with heavy attacks. Due to Edredd being easy to stagger, capitalize on this advantage to land multiple attacks.

Once you’ve dodged the Spinning Soaring Blade Slash, stay close and maintain pressure on Edredd by doing multiple attacks. The key is to match his speed by constantly moving and dodging his blade swings. Edredd's attacks are fast but predictable, learn its patterns and be ready to evade and counter quickly. After each of its attacks, you'll often have a split second to retaliate with your heavy attacks, which can stagger the knight and interrupt its rhythm.

Throughout the fight, maintain a balance between offense and defense. This tactic will gradually wear down his health. Remember to manage your stamina, as constant dodging and attacking can quickly deplete your stamina.

The crossbow gives him an advantage against melee users so it's ideal to stay within attacking distance by going up to him. You'll likely end up getting your HP drained without a fight if you stay far back while you have a melee weapon. You can also equip a shield to block his ranged attacks. At first, his attacks are slow and simple. He swings his greatsword with a powerful slash and you can stay out of his path by rolling to your right side. He holds up the sword with his right arm, and this direction gives you ...

If you have a shield equipped, you can use it to block his incoming attacks or attempt a parry. Both of these methods will give an opening to attack him for maybe 1 or 2 attacks, depending on how fast your attack speed is. Opt for heavy attacks or Ash of War: Giant Hunt, or any Ash of War you prefer. This will cut him off in between combos. This can eventually apply Stagger if you repeatedly hit him with heavy attacks. This boss also has an attack that is similar to the Vacuum Slice that he can combine with ...

You will also notice that this boss tends to do jump attacks. If you can hit him while he's mid-air, you can knock him down and get free hits out of this opportunity. As the fight goes on, this boss will also restore its health using a Flask. You can interrupt him by using a spell like Adula's Moonblade to cancel the animation.

If you find yourself needing to restore HP, make sure to do it at a safe distance and that you have enough time. He may switch to the Crossbow or do a Wide Slash attack that lets him close the gap to perform a melee attack. Another strategy here is to alternate using your shield and go on offense by attacking him as you move to your right. This will give you a moment to attack him from behind for increased damage and also makes you move away from his right weapon swings.

The one of many melee attacks that the Jagged Peak Drake does is a tail sweep. While facing you, it might start to turn around. When it does, it lifts its tail and sweeps it around. This can be easily indicated as it takes a while for the Drake to turn around, so you will need to time your dodge roll right to avoid receiving damage. You can dodge forward to also get closer to it so that you can perform close-range melee attacks on its legs to break its stance to further deal heavy damage to it.

It also has a few attacks where it will be stationed in one location in the area. When you see this, that is your signal to run to the sides to avoid the flames and to catch up to it to deal damage to its sides as it will only direct the flames in front of it. Another attack is when it lets out a roar followed ...

The Jagged Peak Drake has a few leaping attacks that it performs. One of them is its heavy stomps which it will leap into the air, hover a moment, and stomp down heavily onto you. This attack can be indicated when it hovers momentarily in the air. You will need to time your dodge towards its back legs right when it stomps onto the ground, this will avoid the damage and get you closer to attacking it. The next leaping attack is its leaping fire-breathing attack, It will leap up and then breathe out fire when it ...

A good strategy here is to utilize Torrent to make this fight easier, as with all instances of dragon combat. You can ride around the area to evade the dragon's attacks while also chipping off damage by attacking its legs. You can dash away out of harm's way with Torrent, so you can move in and out of combat, making this fight easier if you choose to go on horseback for this fight.

Inflicting Bleed or Frost will cause him to stumble. This is not the same as Stagger, but provides a brief window to disengage, heal, or cancel his attack.

When you first enter the arena, you'll face Midra's human form, a "Wailing Man" armed with a stick. This initial form is much weaker than the main boss but can still cause significant damage through a grab attack or a madness AoE. It is crucial to deplete his health quickly to avoid these attacks. After defeating this form, there's a brief window before Midra transforms into his true form. Use this time to drink the Flask of Wondrous Physick to extend your buffs for the upcoming fight.

Once the transformation is complete, Midra's true form is revealed, and the real challenge begins. His first move will likely be to summon Flame Strands that crawl toward you. To avoid this, time your forward roll just as the attack approaches, then delay a second roll to close the distance. This positioning allows you to land a heavy attack while Midra is recovering, as he is susceptible to being staggered.
By carefully timing your moves and managing your buffs, you can turn the tide in this challenging fight against Midra.

When at close range, Midra will begin swinging his greatsword at you. While he is a slow-moving boss, his attacks are quick and yet, predictable. One of his common attack strings is the Triple Greatsword Swing. He begins with a right overhead swing, followed by a left overhead swing, and ends it again with another right swing in quick succession. This attack can be dodged by going towards his weapon, so you should dodge going to your right, then left, and right again. At the end of this attack string, you should ...

For his second combo, he will pull off a 3-attack string that begins with 2 quick sweeps starting from the left, then right, and followed by a Dash Thrust. The final move in this combo allows him to dash forward which leaves a trail of flames. To dodge this move, roll backward twice for the quick sweeps, then roll forward as he finishes this move. This creates a distance between you and him, and from here, you can cast a spell if you have the FP for it.

Another one of his combos is a 2-attack string where he begins with a left-side swing of his weapon and is followed by a Thrust with a short delay. For this attack, you can dodge by rolling to the left, and then towards him. If you do this successfully, you will be able to get behind him and land another heavy attack. The delay is something that needs to be learned so take your time with this. For the next melee move, you will notice Midra use the nail in his left hand and stab you with it. This Nail Stab attack ...

One of Midra’s most powerful attacks is the Big Flame Explosion. He starts to use this once you reach the second phase when his health drops to about 70%. When you see him rise up above you, it’s a clear sign that the Big Flame Explosion is coming. Once you see him prepare this move, you want to run to the edge of the arena as there's no way of dodging it at close range. Failing to do so can result in high damage, potentially even a one-shot kill, so prioritizing distance is crucial.

In the second phase, Midra will retain his original strings of attacks and will gain new ones. He can now cast a single Flame Strand that travels the same way as his opening attack, but instead of 2 Strands, there's only one here. You can dodge the same way you did previously. The next move begins with Midra firing up his greatsword. You can see the Frenzied Flame covering his weapon and he begins to do a right-step sweep followed closely by a lunge swipe. This move also creates flames on the ground, it doesn't ...

He can also do Explosive Grab Plunge. He will start this attack by flying up in the air and then crashes down onto the ground in an attempt to grab you with his right hand while he plunges the greatsword with his left hand. Watch out for the aftershock where barbs will grow from underneath when he plunges his weapon deeper onto the ground. To dodge this, make sure you look up at his character while he's in mid-air. As Midra is floating, get ready to roll forward right before he hits the ground, then face toward ...

Finally, the longest string of attacks from Midra is a mix of quick and delayed strikes. This attack begins with a left-side sweep followed by 4 strings of delayed and quick attacks that alternate direction. Overall, you can dodge this move in any direction, but the move is more forgiving if you roll toward the origin of the weapon. So if it's coming from the right, you will dodge to the right. Your dodge pattern for this move will go like this:
Dodge to the right for the first sweep
Pause for a brief moment, roll to the left
Do 2 quick rolls to the right, and then left again
Pause here, and wait for the final sweep, then roll to the right

Moving on to his special attack, Midra can also perform Frenzied Gaze, firing multiple beams from a distance. You will notice him pull back his head and then rapidly fire lasers that track you. This move is typically slow and isn't fast enough to keep up with the Tarnished. This works best if you are close to him so make sure that you are near him when he initiates this move. NOTE: Lamenter has a unique instant kill debuff that must be managed throughout the fight. During the clone phase, when the summons vanish at the end of each phase, you will gain a stack of a debuff for every clone that was still alive at the end of the phase. The number of stacks you have is displayed as a ring around your character. You instantly die if the number of stacks reaches 7 during the fight. The stacks do not disappear over time. It is therefore important to kill as many clones as possible during the ...

To manage this phase, systematically attack the clones one at a time until you locate the real Lamenter. The clones can be dealt with quickly, but exercise caution as the distant clones will launch slow-moving Shadow Projectiles at you.

When the clones are inactive, this boss will do a combination of weak punches or jumping attacks. This boss fights with bare fists and is only able to do so at a close range. Both of these moves can be dodged by rolling in either direction (left or right) just before it punches.

Once you identify and attack the real Lamenter, focus on overwhelming it with continuous strikes. Breaking its poise through relentless aggression will give you ample opportunities to deplete its health. By maintaining pressure and carefully navigating the clone phase, you can effectively whittle down Lamenter's health and secure victory in this challenging boss fight.

One of the most accessible parts of the dragon to target is its feet. Since the dragon will be on the ground most of the time, you’ll have opportunities to strike its legs during combat. On the ground, Senessax relies on Lightning Slams and Sweeps. These attacks are powerful but avoidable. When you see the dragon raising its arms, immediately switch to defense and roll back as far as you can. Its lightning melee attacks have a wide damage area, making it crucial to maintain distance. Due to the size of its attack, ...

After the dragon launches an attack and misses, observe its movements closely. If it doesn't seem to attack again soon, take the opportunity to strike its legs and deal heavy damage. Be aware that when the dragon feels pressured by your attacks, it will often use its wings to blow you away, creating distance between you. One strategy that you can use against Ancient Dragon Senessax is to ride Torrent to go in and out of the battle. You can utilize Torrent to easily get out of the boss's reach whenever it attacks, ...

One of the moves that the Ancient Dragon Senessax does is Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear where you see it raise its arms to conjure a lightning bolt, then, it will stab the ground with it to create a lightning AoE damage. This move will have a variation when the boss' health drops to 50%; it will make the same move for the second time after a slight delay. To dodge this move, start by jumping twice while riding Torrent, or you can also do a jump with your character.

Another attack that is worth mentioning is Wingbeat, which is a common move that the boss makes where it flaps both wings to create a wind that will blow you away. This move creates a distance between the two of you and can stagger you when it connects. To avoid this attack, spam roll backwards until you get out of the AoE.

To win the fight against Ancient Dragon Senessax, you need to time your attacks and be patient. Rushing in can lead to immediate death since almost all its attacks are very powerful. Regularly switch between defense and offense, evading more than attacking. Patience is critical; wait for the right moments to attack, and gradually, you’ll lower its health.

Bayle also has several powerful Fire and Lightning breath attacks. One is an arena-wide attack, where Bayle sweeps Fire and Lightning from one side to the other. When you first engage the Dancer of Ranah, one of her initial moves is the Double-Spinning Slash. Since this boss is prone to getting staggered, we recommend casting Greatblade Phalanx as soon as you enter the arena. This way, you can charge toward her and the launched spell can break her poise briefly, and you will be free to attack. This boss usually backs away frequently either by jumping backward or rolling.

One of the moves that she will do is when she charges at you and performs two quick slashes. This attack can be countered by rolling back twice or by rolling back once and then countering with an attack just before she executes the second slash. At the end of each attack pattern, this boss will disengage by any means available to her.

When cornered or under pressure, the Dancer of Ranah often resorts to her Wide Flame Attack. During this move, she claps her hands and releases multiple small fireballs in an arching direction. You can spot this move when you see the fire light up in each of her hands; your best strategy is to run away from her the moment that you see this. Alternatively, you can roll back multiple times until the flames dissipate. Then, be ready to go back in as the flames go out.

At close range, she also uses Basic slashes and Jumping slashes. While these attacks are predictable and relatively easy to evade, it's important not to become overconfident. Her attacks, though easy to read, can deal good damage if they connect. Stay alert and continue to dodge while looking for openings to strike. Since this boss overuses rolling dodge, you want to consider using long-reaching armament to punish her when she's trying to roll away mid-sequence.

Throughout the battle, maintain a balance between offense and defense. Be aggressive most of the time, especially when she is vulnerable after her attacks, but switch to a defensive approach when she initiates her flaming attacks. Staying too aggressive during her fire-based moves can lead to damage. Overall, the Dancer of Ranah’s attacks are predictable and provide plenty of opportunities to counter. Focus on staggering her with consistent melee attacks and take advantage of the openings this creates. By keeping ...

The Knight will plummet in your direction and chop down with the cleaver, followed closely by a spin attack, then the horse will charge toward you, and then the knight will do another spin attack. There's a chance that the last 2 of this combo will be repeated where the horse will charge again, and the knight will do another spin. You can dodge this attack ...

The next combo from this boss is the Cleaver Chop attack. This is when he chops down with his weapon using both hands while he's on horseback. Be very careful as he can combine this move with quick sweeps on either side. There's a wind-up for this attack pattern, so make sure you keep an eye on his arm movements. When it comes to the chop down, you want to roll forward as soon as he strikes, then, for the quick sweeps, you will roll towards the origin of the weapon. You can either do it to the side (left or right) ...

The next move from this boss is the Cleaver Throw where he uses his weapon as a boomerang. During this attack, you can get hit twice if you're not careful. The first one is when he throws it toward you, and then the hit as it comes back to him. You will want to roll during the first instance and keep out of the path of the boomerang as the cleaver returns to him. The Putrescent Knight likes to disengage and he can do it quickly because of his horse. There might be a few openings in combat but you just have to be ...

By the time you get its HP to below 60-70%, this boss will activate its PHASE 2. This is when he will slowly rise and cast Vortex of Putrescence. This attack creates several globs of putrescence all around the knight, which burst into ghostflame and travels outward if it lands on the ground. To dodge this attack, you will need to jump and get the timing right. It's going to pay off a lot to practice this because the move is arena-wide and there's nowhere for you to run while this attack is active. Another ...

Aside from these two, the other skill that he can use during Phase 2 is Mass of Putrescence where he fires a glob of putrescence, which erupts into a ghostflame stream that travels forward. This is a move that he can combine with his basic attacks or basic combos especially when you're far away from him. Don't be too greedy if this boss is too far away. Melee users need to take their time to close the gap so they can strike back. The knight's attacks inflict very high damage and can defeat you with only a few ...

Remain observant of your surroundings throughout the fight, as the horse will charge at you randomly. Even when at a distance from the knight, stay alert, as the knight will throw its blade like a boomerang, forcing you to dodge again.

St. Trina's Smile.title: St. Trina's Smile
intro: St. Trina's Smile is a Talisman in Elden Ring. It is a brand-new Talisman in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. It increases attack power when the sleep status effect is in the vicinity. Players can use Talismans in Elden Ring to boost a variety of Stats.
where: Where to find St. Trina's Smile:
Obtained as a drop upon defeating a hostile NPC, Thiollier. See Shadow of the Erdtree Map
Thiollier only becomes hostile if you pursue St. Trina and Thiollier's quest. Please visit their pages for the quest guide.

St. Trina's Blossom.title: St. Trina's Blossom
intro: St. Trina's Blossom is a Helm in Elden Ring. It is a brand-new Helm in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. St. Trina's Blossom is not part of a set, and can be obtained once players complete St. Trina's questline. St. Trina's Blossom protects the player's head by applying various defensive properties, it also changes the appearance as well when it is equipped. Some armor pieces may be available to both genders, but may be slightly different for male and female characters.
where: The St. Trina's Blossom Helm can be found at:
Initiating Thiollier's sidequest is not required to obtain this item.

St. Trina Disciple's Cookbook (3).title: St. Trina Disciple's Cookbook (3)
intro: St. Trina Disciple's Cookbook [3] is a Cookbook in Elden Ring. St. Trina Disciple's Cookbook [3] is a brand new Cookbook in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. Cookbooks are records of crafting techniques that players can use to learn how to craft a wide variety of items.

Velvet Sword of St Trina.title: Velvet Sword of St Trina
intro: Velvet Sword of St. Trina is a Straight Sword in Elden Ring. It is a brand new Straight Sword in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. The Velvet Sword of St Trina scales primarily with Strength, Dexterity and Intelligence and is a good Weapon for players looking for magic damage straight sword. This also has a strong base physical damage of 95. It produces eternal sleep build-up and a skill named Mists of Eternal Sleep that releases a cloud of purple mist when you perform a slash.
where: The Velvet Sword of St Trina weapon can be found at the following location:

Stone Coffin Fissure: From the Fissure Cross site of grace, walk immediately north-west to the closest giant coffin that's tilted nearly vertical. Climb down to a ledge that passes underneath the brick platform nearest the site of grace. The sword is in a small cave network there and guarded by several putrescent oozes. See Shadow of the Erdtree Map
